stem.text: Find the interval of convergence of the power series \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{8 \left(x - 4\right)^{n}}{3^{n}} \). Use the ratio test for the interior and justify the behaviour at each endpoint.

answer_key.label: The interval of convergence is \( 1 < x < 7 \).

worked_solution.text: The series converges when \( \frac{\left|x - 4\right|}{3} < 1 \), that is \( \left|x - 4\right| < 3 \), so \( 1 < x < 7 \).

At \( x = 7 \) the series is \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} 8 \), which diverges by the nth term test, since every term equals 8. At \( x = 1 \) the series is \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} 8 (-1)^n \), which diverges by the nth term test, since its terms do not approach 0.
The interval of convergence is \( 1 < x < 7 \).

options.label: The interval of convergence is \( x < 7 \).
options.derivation: the absolute value dropped when solving, so x - 4 < 3 was kept as the whole solution and only the endpoint 7 tested

options.label: The interval of convergence is \( 1 \le x < 7 \).

options.label: The interval of convergence is \( 1 \le x \le 7 \).
